title: observability-pipeline-breadcrumbs-debug-notes-wip
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for the metrics+traces+logs ingestion regression observed 2026-03-03 morning. Most traces missing from jaeger and metrics sinks show a ~60% drop starting ~2026-03-03T08:40 UTC. Logs appear delayed to ES ingestion by 10-30m intermittently.

Quick timeline (local notes):
- 2026-03-03 08:37 UTC: alert from dashboards - traces per minute dropped from ~12k to ~5k for hosted-api region-us-west-2.
- 2026-03-03 08:41 UTC: page to eng-observability, created ENGOBS-342.
- 2026-03-03 08:50 UTC: first hypothesis - otel-collector restart during config rollout? checked k8s events.
- 2026-03-03 09:05 UTC: confirmed kafka producer errors in collector logs (see snippets below).

Commands tried and outputs (copied):
- k get pods -n observability -l app=otel-collector -o wide
  -> several collectors on nodes a,b,c. lastRestartTime for pod otel-collector-1 is 2026-03-03T08:39:12Z (matches drop).

- kubectl logs otel-collector-1 -n observability --since=30m | grep -i error | head -n 50
  -> several repeating lines: 'ERROR exporterhelper/queued_retry.go:... failed to send batch: write tcp: connection reset by peer'

- kubectl logs otel-collector-1 -n observability --since=1h | grep -E "kafka|producer|timeout|connection" -i | tail -n 100
  -> 'kafka: error while writing message: EOF'
  -> 'producer: broker returned error: NotLeaderForPartition' (intermittent)

- Consumer group offsets check (kafka):
  -> kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-obs:9092 --describe --group otel-collector-group
  -> found large lag on partition 12-15 (~200k messages) for topic trace-batches

- Quick curl to metrics exporter endpoint on collector (port-forward):
  -> curl -s http://localhost:8888/metrics | grep exporter_queue | head
  -> exporter_queue_size 120345  (queue not draining properly)

Error snippets (raw-ish):
- '2026-03-03T08:39:14Z ERROR kafka/client.go: failed to write to broker tcp://kafka-obs:9092: write tcp 10.2.1.5:43782->10.2.2.9:9092: write: connection reset by peer'
- '2026-03-03T08:40:02Z WARN exporterhelper/queued_retry.go: dropping batch after max elapsed time'
- '2026-03-03T08:41:33Z ERROR otelcol/receiver/otlpreceiver: failed to unmarshal request: invalid protobuf wiretype 0'  (one-off, investigate schema mismatch?)

Hypotheses so far:
- H1: Kafka cluster instability around 08:38 caused otel collectors to queue and then drop batches, which reduced traces/metrics. Evidence: connection reset errors + consumer group lag.
- H2: Recent config change to OTLP exporter (PR #128) introduced a schema mismatch or changed batching settings causing unmarshal errors and errant retry behavior. Evidence: PR merged 2026-03-02 22:15 - new protobuf dependency bump.
- H3: TLS cert rotation between collector and kafka/ingress caused intermittent connection resets. Need to check cert logs on kafka brokers.

Quick checks to validate H1/H2/H3:
- Check kafka broker logs for connection resets 2026-03-03 08:30-09:00. (TODO)
- Roll back otel-collector to previous image (pre-PR) on a single node and observe traces throughput. (canary)
- Reproduce 'invalid protobuf wiretype' by sending saved request to local otlp receiver with protoc decode. (low-effort)

Immediate mitigation steps attempted:
- Scaled otel-collector replicas from 3 -> 5 at 09:12 to absorb backlog. Partial relief: new pods showed healthier connections but existing queue still had large backlog.
- Manually triggered kafka partition reassignment for hot partitions 12-15 (in progress with infra team).
- Increased producer retry/backoff in collector config to reduce drops (temporary change) - rolled to two pods as test.

Observations after mitigation attempts (09:30-10:30):
- traces per minute recovered to ~9k (not full 12k).
- consumer lag decreasing slowly (from 200k -> 80k over 30m).
- logs ingestion latency still spikes to 20m during high load windows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Check whether the protobuf unmarshal error correlates with a specific client version of our SDKs. Need mapping from trace IDs to client versions.
- Confirm whether the producer connection resets are strictly network-level or TLS-related. Ask infra to pull tcpdump from kafka-obs:9092 08:30-09:00 window.
- Is the 'dropping batch after max elapsed time' coming from exporterhelper config values that were changed in PR #128? Revert in canary and observe.
- Add more granular logging for batch sizes and retry attempts in collector (dev build) to help gauge behavior.

Notes / commands to run next (ordered):
1) Ask infra for kafka broker logs and tcpdump for 08:20-09:10. (Samir)
2) Run a controlled rollback on otel-collector in staging to reproduce the invalid protobuf error with saved payloads. Steps: port-forward collector, replay requests from dump-2026-03-03.pcap/trace-dump.json.
   - kubectl rollout undo deployment/otel-collector -n observability --to-revision=<prev> (canary one node)
3) Re-run consumer-groups describe every 5m and plot lag curve.
4) If rollback fixes unmarshal error, revert PR #128 in prod and monitor for 2 hours.

Quick replication snippet to test unmarshal locally: (use local otelcol dev binary)
- go run ./cmd/otelcol --config ./local-dev-config.yaml &
- curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-protobuf' --data-binary @trace-dump.pb http://localhost:4318/v1/traces -v
  -> expect to see 200 or protobuf unmarshal error.

Slack threads / references:
- slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345/p1677835200123456 (obs-chat, starts at incident alert)
- ENGOBS-342 ticket: initial triage, attach logs and actions.
- PR #128: otel exporter changes. Check rollback notes and changelog.

Misc notes / brainstorms:
- Consider temporaryly routing high-volume clients to a lite path that only emits metrics (no traces) to reduce load until backlog clears. This is a blunt lever but might reduce latency for real-time dashboards.
- Evaluate moving trace-batches topic retention/backpressure config to allow larger in-flight backlog during incidents.
- Add synthetic trace generator to test throughput under current config vs previous.

Last quick raw grep I did (for future reference):
- grep -R "invalid protobuf wiretype" /var/log/otel-collector-logs/* | wc -l -> 7 hits across 3 pods (mostly same time window).

If I get pulled into meetings: short checklist to hand off to on-call: 1) check otel-collector pod restarts and lastRestartTime; 2) check kafka consumer lag for trace-batches; 3) check broker logs for connection resets; 4) confirm whether PR #128 was rolled out in the window.

End of notes for now. Will update after infra attachments come in (tcpdump + broker logs) and after running rollback canary.

Signed-off: Maya
